enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 420 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

 - Pacific cold front will bring scattered showers and
   thunderstorms this afternoon and evening. Breezy to windy into
   Monday.

 - Storms will be capable of heavy rain, in particular the Gila
   Wilderness. A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of Grant
   and Hidalgo Counties. Storms may also produce damaging winds
   and a brief, weak tornado.

 - Quieter and drier weather will prevail after Monday with
   temperatures remaining seasonable. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 935 AM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

Unsettled weather is forecast for the short-term. Plentiful
moisture has moved over the region, exhibited by our 12z (!) RAOB,
which collected 1.21" of PWs. Normal for early Nov is about 0.4".
This is courtesy of the subtropical jet being pulled northward
ahead of a deep longwave trough moving into the Great Basin today.
We'll be in the right entrance region of the jet with good speed
shear and modest instability. Only about 500 J/kg of SBCAPE are
modeled for this afternoon with higher values to the east into SE
NM. Excellent 0-6km shear of 50kts is modeled by the REFS later 
today as the jet streak moves overhead. All the cloud cover 
streaming overhead may inhibit how unstable we get later today, 
but the favorable jet/frontal dynamics should help overcome that 
in terms of convective initiation. 

The Pacific front will push through S NM this evening with a wave
of showers and storms ahead of it, forming what appears to be a 
squall line. Strong-severe wind gusts are possible from this 
convective line as it progresses W to E into the overnight. SPC
has increased our severe risk for today/tonight with a portion of
Otero and Sierra counties now in a SLGT for damaging winds and an
isolated tornado. 0-1km SRH should exceed 100 m2/s2 in some areas
through the evening, favoring northern areas for the marginal
tornado threat. Eastern NM is most likely to see tornadoes through
tonight. The rain/storm threat will diminish for far west TX as
the best dynamics track to the northeast. 

Flood Watch remains in effect for the Gila through the evening
where moisture and jet dynamics are most favorable. Repeated
rounds of rain are forecast with isolated amounts of 1-2" and a
few instances of flash flooding, especially in areas that have
received heavy rainfall recently. The flood threat lowers as you
head south and east. Rain chances largely end by the early AM Mon.

Breezy to strong synoptic winds are forecast as well with this
system, increasing to near advisory level in the Gila this
afternoon, shifting E overnight to the San Andres/Organs and then
the Sacs. The strongest winds are expected in the Sacs with gusts
to 60-70 mph possible along ridges and east slopes into the day on
Mon. Wind headlines have been posted to reflect these hazards.
Elsewhere, breezy conditions are expected with gusts to around 40
mph, continuing into Mon mainly E of the RGV. 

Dry and calmer winds after Mon with seasonal temps under quasi-
zonal flow.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 420 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

A band of showers with embedded thunderstorms is moving west to
east across Southern New Mexico. This band is associated with a
Pacific cold front sweeping across the area which will continue to
impact the region through 07Z tonight. Main feature beside 
showers will be strong winds gusting up to 30 knots from the west 
southwest. Post frontal west winds of 20 to 25 knots will occur 
after 12Z Monday at all TAF sites. Winds over mtn ranges will be
quite strong with wind warnings out for the Sacramento Mountains 
on Monday. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 935 AM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast through the period. Pacific
front brings a wave of showers/storms through the evening, some
producing high rain rates and damaging winds. Flood threat is
highest in the Gila with the severe threat across northern areas.
Rain chances diminish for areas to south and east. Breezy SW 
winds develop this afternoon, shifting W overnight. Breezy winds 
progress eastward on Mon with lighter winds out west. Winds
subside for Tue, staying light for the rest of the week. No chance
of rain starting Mon with cooler temps.

Min RHs range from 40-80% today, then 30-50%. Vent rates will be
good to excellent through Mon, then mostly poor on Tue.
